findings.summary: Adam Boehler DFC-to-Affinity pipeline: college roommate led DFC with 60B lending authority, built Gulf relationships that became Affinity investor base
findings.detail: Adam Boehler was Jared Kushner Harvard summer roommate. Served as first CEO of U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) Dec 2019-Jan 2021 with 60B lending authority. DFC invests in developing countries to counter Chinese Belt and Road. Geographic overlap with Affinity target markets (Middle East, Africa, South/Southeast Asia). Boehler traveled with Kushner to Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar in 2020-2021 on delegations leading to Abraham Accords. American Oversight obtained 423-page FOIA of Boehler-Kushner communications during COVID pandemic. Dec 2024 nominated as Special Presidential Envoy for Hostage Affairs, withdrew March 2025 after being sidelined, reappointed April 2025 as SGE.

findings.summary: Boehler-Kushner 423-page DFC FOIA contains ONLY COVID pandemic communications; no mentions of Saudi, UAE, Qatar, investment, sovereign wealth, or Middle East
findings.detail: American Oversight FOIA (DocumentCloud 21044267, 423 pages, released Aug 2021) covers DFC CEO Boehler communications with Kushner and associates. Content is entirely COVID-19 pandemic response: ventilator allocation, PPE procurement, testing logistics, Google statements, media inquiries. Avi Berkowitz appears extensively but only in WH coronavirus response role. 15-20 percent redacted under FOIA b5 and b6 exemptions. No mentions of: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, PIF, sovereign wealth, investment fund, MBS, Gulf, Middle East, Israel, Abraham Accords, Gerson, real estate, Affinity, Serbia, Albania, DFC projects, BUILD Act, or OPIC. Key implication: Gulf investment relationship-building either occurred through other channels not captured in this FOIA, or the critical relationship-building period was outside the March-April 2020 window covered.
